data.title: MacKenzie Realty Capital Holds Annual Meeting and Elects Directors
data.description:
MacKenzie Realty Capital, Inc. ( (MKZR) ) has provided an update.

MacKenzie Realty Capital, Inc., a Maryland corporation, held its annual meeting on November 16, 2026, with proposals to elect four directors and ratify Baker Tilly, LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2027. A quorum was reached with 1,508,476 shares, or 54.37% of shares outstanding and eligible to vote, present.

All four director nominees were elected to serve until the 2027 annual meeting and successor qualification, with more than 75% of shares present voting for each. Stockholders ratified Baker Tilly, LLP, with 1,350,510 votes for, 122,666 against and 35,300 abstentions; 89.53% of shares present voted for ratification, and no broker non-votes were cast.

data.title: CRH plc Announces Early Results for Arcosa Note Offers
data.description:

On November 19, 2026, CRH plc announced early results for cash tender offers and private exchange offers covering Arcosa Inc.’s 4.375% senior notes due 2029 and 6.875% senior notes due 2032. CRH America Finance offered cash for any and all notes or exchanges for up to $1 billion aggregate principal amount of new notes fully and unconditionally guaranteed by CRH plc.

data.title: First Real Estate Investment Terminates Westwood Plaza Sale Agreement
data.description:
First Real Estate Investment of New Jersey ( (FREVS) ) has issued an update.

On May 26, 2026, the Trust entered into an agreement to sell 100% of its ownership interests in Westwood Plaza, a shopping center in Westwood, New Jersey, to an affiliate of Regency Centers Corporation for $28,800,000, subject to the agreement’s terms and conditions. On September 23, 2026, the parties extended the inspection period to November 17, 2026; on November 17, the purchaser requested an extension to November 20, which the seller declined.

The purchaser’s right to continue due diligence lapsed when the inspection period expired, and the agreement was terminated on November 17, 2026. The $1,200,000 escrowed deposit will be returned under the agreement, and the seller incurred no termination penalty.

data.title: Pure Cycle Reports Fiscal 2026 Revenue and Income Growth
data.description:
Pure Cycle ( (PCYO) ) has issued an update.

On November 18, 2026, Pure Cycle reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $35.7 million, up 37%, with growth in its lot sales, water and wastewater, and single-family rental segments. Operating income rose 75% to $13.4 million, while net income increased 9% to $14.2 million, or $0.59 per diluted share, despite a $4.7 million decline in oil and gas royalty income.

During fiscal 2026, accelerated Sky Ranch development left Phase 2C 98% complete, Phase 2D 89% complete and Phase 2E 34% complete as of August 31, 2026. The Board decided against further rental-home investment beyond the existing portfolio and construction contracts, determined to sell the rental homes and reserved lots in an orderly manner, and temporarily suspended share repurchases because of the pending proxy contest.

data.title: Vizsla Silver Revises Panuco First Silver Production Target to H2 2028
data.description:
Vizsla Silver ( (TSE:VZLA) ) has provided an update.

On Nov. 19, 2026, Vizsla Silver reported continued development of its wholly owned Panuco silver-gold project in Mexico, with work focused on construction readiness. M3 Engineering & Technology had completed approximately 50% of engineering, and approximately 85% of contemplated process-plant equipment had been ordered.

Three development contracts had been awarded for engineering procurement and construction management, mine design and equipment supply, while the main mining contract remained to be awarded. The company also said it was working with Mexican federal authorities and third-party security advisers on preparations for a phased return to site.

Vizsla revised its targeted first silver-production date to the second half of 2028 from the second half of 2027, citing expectations for permitting, site readiness and construction timing. It committed an initial US$5 million to a planned Vizsla Foundation intended to support education, health and economic development in communities surrounding Panuco.

The company did not update the operating, capital or economic parameters from its November 2025 feasibility study and said it had made no production decision. The revised timeline marked a one-year delay to the targeted production start while development planning and security preparations continued.

data.title: Lisata Therapeutics Implements One-for-Fifteen Reverse Stock Split
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Lisata Therapeutics ( (LSTA) ).

On November 19, 2026, Lisata Therapeutics filed an amendment implementing a one-for-fifteen reverse stock split of its common stock. The action followed stockholder approval at the company’s November 9 annual meeting, after which the board selected the one-for-fifteen ratio from the approved range.

Under the announced terms, every 15 shares would be combined into one, reducing issued and outstanding shares from approximately 10.8 million to approximately 0.7 million. Ownership percentages would remain generally unchanged, while fractional shares would be paid in cash and outstanding convertible or exercisable securities adjusted accordingly.

data.title: SmartKem Board Approves 1-for-5 Reverse Stock Split
data.description:
SmartKem ( (SMTK) ) has issued an announcement.

On November 19, 2026, SmartKem said its board approved a 1-for-5 reverse stock split after shareholder authorization at the June 23 annual meeting. The announcement described the reverse split as supporting continued Nasdaq listing and combining every five outstanding shares into one, while leaving authorized shares and proportional ownership unchanged apart from fractional-share treatment.

The reverse split also called for proportionate adjustments to equity awards, warrants and other securities convertible into or exchangeable for common stock, including applicable exercise and conversion prices. Fractional shares were to be rounded up to the nearest whole share, while shareholders’ positions would be adjusted automatically through brokers or nominees.
